can_answer: partly: the file can compare the frequency of reported crashes across clock-time periods, but it has no traffic-volume or travel-exposure denominator and therefore cannot establish individual road-user danger or crash risk.
metric: Police-reported crashes per calendar clock-hour opportunity, grouped into day (06:00-19:59), night (20:00-23:59 and 01:00-05:59), and records stamped exactly 00:00:00 (shown separately as possible default-time records).
denominator: For each group, the number of clock-hours in that group multiplied by calendar days in the included complete years 2013-2025 (14 hours/day for day, 9 for night, and 1 for 00:00); this corrects for group duration but not for traffic or travel exposure.
population: One row per police-reported NYC motor-vehicle crash with nonmissing DATE crash_date and TIME crash_time in complete calendar years represented in the file.
filters: Keep rows with a valid DATE crash_date and TIME crash_time
Keep records stamped 00:00:00 but show them in a separate group rather than assigning them to night
years: Complete-boundary years 2013-2025, determined by observed minimum and maximum crash dates within each year.
grouping: Day (06:00-19:59), night excluding exactly 00:00 (20:00-23:59 and 01:00-05:59), and the separate recorded-00:00:00 group.
data_check_and_decisions: The complete-boundary years contain 2,132,218 dated rows, all with nonmissing times; date coverage is partial in 2012 (July 1-December 31) and 2026 (January 1-June 11), so those 136,969 rows are excluded. No crash dates or times are NULL, and DATE/TIME types cannot hold blank strings, unknown words, or impossible calendar/time values. Exactly 23,787 complete-year rows (1.1158%) are stamped 00:00:00, with an obvious increase in that pileup from 2016 onward; because this may be a default rather than true midnight, retain these rows as their own displayed group, not as night. The full-boundary check is based on first/last observed dates and cannot verify reporting completeness on every intervening day.
limitations: This is a comparison of police-reported crash counts per clock-hour opportunity, not crashes per vehicle, traveler, trip, mile, or hour of travel. The file has no traffic-volume or exposure measure. The exact-00:00 pileup may reflect default times; it is displayed separately. Only complete-boundary years 2013-2025 are used, based on observed date endpoints rather than proof of complete reporting for every day.
